title: Binary sequential calibration with arbitrary causal randomized predictors
summary: Each round, the predictor outputs a probability while the environment simultaneously selects a binary outcome. Both may use the past, but the environment cannot observe the current realized prediction first. The objective is standard cumulative absolute calibration error.

metric.base_expression: $$\operatorname{Cal}_T=\sum_{p\in\{p_1,\ldots,p_T\}}\left|\sum_{t:p_t=p}(y_t-p_t)\right|.$$ Sum only over distinct forecast probabilities actually used. This is neither per-round absolute error nor binned approximate calibration.
metric.normalization: Group exactly equal prediction values and sum absolute deviations. Do not divide by T.
metric.finiteness_conditions: The triangle inequality places calibration error in $[0,T]$.
description_paragraphs:
$$
\operatorname{Cal}_T=\sum_{p\in\{p_1,\ldots,p_T\}}\left|\sum_{t:p_t=p}(y_t-p_t)\right|.
$$
The outer sum runs only over distinct prediction probabilities actually used. The criterion is neither per-round absolute error nor an approximation after binning.

operations.query_signature: The predictor chooses $p_t\in[0,1]$ while the adversary simultaneously chooses $y_t\in\{0,1\}$. Both may use past predictions and outcomes, but the adversary choosing $y_t$ cannot see the current realized randomized prediction $p_t$. After both act, $p_t,y_t$ is revealed. No true conditional mean or privileged prediction interface is supplied. Past feedback may be stored and reused computationally; no additional historical or sample queries are available beyond the explicitly declared interface.
